neighborhood_overview:
The Barceloneta is a triangular spit of land that cuts into the sea boats in the old harbour, or Barcelona’s Port Vell, on one side, and sandy beaches on the other. The neighbourhood, with its narrow, rectilinear streets, was built on a military grid structure to provide accommodation for the former inhabitants of La Ribera.

The Barceloneta was once the home of fishermen, people associated with the fishing trade and the metal industry, and is now one of the city’s most visited and popular districts. In 1988, in pre-Olympic days, the decision was taken to demolish the old beachfront restaurants, known as xiringuitos, and public baths, heralding a process of opening the city up to the sea and the modernisation of an area which now offers first-class beaches as the main attraction for its visitors.

On the sand and inside the neighbourhood, rows of restaurants and bars combine with the traditional images of locals sitting in their chairs in the street and narrow balco

It is bordered by Avenida de la República Argentina, Calle Claudi Sabadell, Calle de Marmellà, Calle de Roca i Batlle, Padre Fidel Fita Street, Calle de Musitu, Calle de Bertrán, Calle de Balmes, the round of General Mitre and Lesseps Square.

neighborhood_overview:
The Gothic Quarter (Catalan: Barri Gòtic and Spanish: Barrio Gótico) is the centre of the old city of Barcelona. It stretches from La Rambla to Via Laietana, and from the Mediterranean seafront to Ronda de Sant Pere. It is a part of Ciutat Vella district.
Despite several changes undergone in the 19th and early 20th century, many of the buildings date from Medieval times, some from as far back as the Roman settlement of Barcelona. Remains of the squared Roman Wall can be seen around Tapineria and Sots-Tinent Navarro to the north, Avinguda de la Catedral and Plaça Nova to the west and Carrer de la Palla to the south. El Call, the medieval Jewish quarter, is located within this area too.
The Barri Gòtic retains a labyrinthine street plan, with many small streets opening out into squares. Most of the quarter is closed to regular traffic although open to service vehicles and taxis.

El Raval is a very lively place due to its local lifestyle and offers all the services: food stores, supermarkets, bars, museums, restaurants, film library, gym, beauty center...

The beautiful neighbourhood known as the Gothic Quarter is so called because it used to be the Roman village and thus has some remnants of its glorious past. These days because of the constant modernization it is easy to spot an ancient building right next to one built in the 90s. It is this mix of old and new that brings people from all over the world to stay in the Gothic Quarter.
You will be spoilt for choice of restaurants and bars, especially around Plaça Reial which is always full day and night. The night-life in the Gothic Quarter is lively to say the least and you will always find somewhere to have a drink or a dance. Calle Ferran, which is just to one side of Plaça Reial and leads up to Plaça Sant Jaume with its imposing government buildings is also good for bars and cafes.

name: Cozy Bright & Centric Ramblas Space, Leafy Terrace
description:
Welcome to our Home, an oasis in the heart of Barcelona that we love to share with our guests!
Spread across 90 sqm, this newly renovated gem boasts two large double bedrooms with King/Queen beds, ensuring a restful stay. With two modern bathrooms, getting ready for a day of exploring is a breeze. Relax in the bright and airy living room or step out onto our charming green and leafy terrace to savor the city's atmosphere.
Experience Barcelona's allure from this comfortable and stylish retreat!
neighborhood_overview:
Raval is a multicultural mosaic of people from all over the world.
Here, Barcelona’s modernity is fused with the past of the Barrio Chino. At one time it was one of the most densely populated districts of Barcelona, but now after many depopulation plans, the city is removing the underdeveloped parts and replacing them with parks, plazas, cultural centers, and much more.
This used to be an uncomfortable area of Barcelona, but it has turned itself around.
It’s now very charming with many independent shops and home of La Boquería Market, Las Ramblas, El Gran Teatro del Liceo, Museo Marítimo, Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Barcelona (MACBA), Centro de Cultura Contemporánea de Barcelona (CCCB), La Filmoteca, Antic Hospital of Santa Creu, music clubs, small galleries and ateliers, modernist bars and restaurant such as the Confitería, the Almirall or the Marsella.
host_about:
Hello Travelers!

We are Barbara and Emiliano, a couple from Italy now based in Barcelona since more than fifteen years after having lived and traveled in several countries in the last 25 years.

We are passionate about travels, photography and food, and we love to meet people, so we decided to host and share our home with guests who visit this wonderful city, connect with people from different culture and, why not, share also a succulent dinner :). We also love nature, animals and outdoor life in general and we enjoy cooking, reading, music and cinema.

From our travel experiences we've come to know what we love about Airbnb: a clean welcoming home and warm hospitality, awesome hosts, interesting neighborhood, and be able to feel like being at home even when you're 10,000 miles from Home; so our goal is to provide the same to every guest we host and we hope they leave with special memories.

We'll be happy to provide you with tips regarding restaurants and nice things to see and do in Barcelona (expecially in our fantastic barrio) and make your stay in Barcelona better.

neighborhood_overview:
The neighborhood of Gràcia is just one stop up from the top of Passeig de Gràcia but it feels like a whole different world. Gràcia was an independent town until the late 19th century and even now the community is small and tight. The people are exceedingly proud of their roots, they don't say they come from Barcelona, they say they are from Gràcia.
The area is popular with artists and a generally bohemian crowd. It also has a high ethnic population and the highest concentration of foreign restaurants in Barcelona. Plaça del Sol is the most renowned area of the neighborhood, it's lined with terrace cafés and at night this is where the people convene to drink and be merry.

This place is good for people who want to live a real local experience.

The Eixample, which translates as "widening" because it is the newest part of the city, is a large area north of Plaça Catalunya to the left and Passeig de Gràcia to the right.
The Eixample is famous because there you can find most of Barcelona's art nouveau masterpieces and because it is a high class residential area with many shops.
The right side of the Eixample is the oldest and therefore has a more impressive architecture, although in reality there is no great difference between the two parts.

The Passeig de Gràcia is located in the heart of the Eixample and divides it into two: "the left Eixample" and "the right Eixample".
Here you can find the best international designer stores, such as Chanel and MaxMara. In addition, along this street are La Pedrera and Casa Batlló, two of Gaudí's typical dreamed buildings. This place also houses several interesting art galleries and, if art is what attracts you, then do not miss visiting the Antoni Tàpies Foundation,

Barcelona architecture is, in reality, an attraction in itself. Just stroll around the city, especially through our neighborhood: "the Eixample", and you'll find an endless amount of fascinating buildings and unexpected treasures.

neighborhood_overview:
Barcelona architecture is, in reality, an attraction in itself. Just stroll around the city, especially through our neighborhood: "the Eixample", and you'll find an endless amount of fascinating buildings and unexpected treasures.

From Roman times to the Gothic period to the Catalan Art Nouveau, "modernisme," Barcelona's architecture naturally transmits the city's rich history. It speaks for eras of varying prosperity and decline, for fervent Catalan nationalism or subjugation to the central government, for Expos, Olympic Games, Cultural Forums and more.

The two most important styles of Barcelona architecture are Catalan Gothic, a medieval style, and Modernisme, a turn of the 20th century movement protagonized by Antoni Gaudí.

host_about:
I am Danish expat in Barcelona working for a large IT company. 
In my free time I enjoy sports and exploring this amazing city. 
Best places to eat in bcn 
Ziryab Fusion Tapas Bar they are good and make tapas that are mix of Arabic and Spanish food. Really delicious. 
Tickets bar should be amazing (I never tried it). I heard it's a former Michelin chef who runs it. 
El nacional is a beautiful eating place where you have 5 or 6 different restaurant focusing on e.g. fish, meat or tapas. 
Elsa y fred is good as well (french restaurant)
Teresa Charles and flax and kale for great vegetarian food.
Sensi consist of a couple restaurant next to each other. Great tapas place. My favorites are sensi gourmet and sensi bistro tapes.
Vinitus is great as well for tapas. 
You have a street called carrer de blai full of pinxo restaurants that is quite cheap. 
Robadora is a good tapas place as well. 
If you want to try something different there is a place called Cape diem by the beach which serve asian food and they serve in like a club-like environment with DJ and dark lights. 
In the area around El Born Centre de cultura you have several good restaurants for tapas like eldiset and bormuth. :)

neighborhood_overview: As Barcelona’s most recognizable neighborhood, Eixample is a late 19th-century urban development known for its dazzling Art Nouveau architecture. Named the "Expansion" in Catalan, the district is characterized by its geometric grid layout and is located north of Plaça de Catalunya. Admire Modernist townhouses that line the main streets, or stop by a cozy sidewalk café to people-watch while sipping a café con leche or cortado. Don’t miss the chance to visit Casa Batlló, Casa Milà, and the unfinished Sagrada Familia, all stunning attractions designed by world-famous Catalan architect, Antoni Gaudí. With stylish boutiques, upscale eateries, and more all within walking distance, spend your days exploring everything that this unparalleled neighborhood has to offer.

name: A beautiful room in Guinardo
description:
Hello everybody, welcome to our little house. Our home is like a sanctuary where we take care of our plants, the food we eat, and the vibes.

It is not located in the center of Barcelona, but it's a quiet neighborhood and it's very close to the Barcelona mountains.

PS: Even if you'll have a bunk bed in the dormitory, the use of the room is totally private and for a single person during your stay with us.

PS2: The view is not from the apartment but at 10 minutes' distance walking.
host_about:
Hi everyone!

I'm Edgar, welcome to my place! 

I like to have people from anywhere as long as they can follow the small everyday routines and organization. As a permaculture lover, I like our guests to respect the ecosystem while they are with us. It simply means to use our amenties with moderation and conciousness. We also recycle with separated bins. Taking care of the appartment where we live and the people (we are 3), is also very important. 

Another important thing for us is that we are not a hostel. We want you to have the best experience with all the comfort that our little home can give you. But as we are are going to live with you for a few days we also like to be aknowledged (just a simple "Hi! How are you?" is enough). The main thing is that we want to feel that you are sharing with us your experience.  

Thanks for reading. 
We are looking forward to meeting you!

Admire Modernist townhouses that line the main streets, or stop by a cozy sidewalk café to people-watch while sipping a café con leche or cortado. With stylish boutiques, upscale eateries, and more all within walking distance, spend your days exploring everything that this unparalleled neighborhood has to offer.

name: ¡Precioso Oasis en el medio de Barcelona City!
description:
Welcome to Rumi's World! I open the doors of my home to anyone who seeks harmony, peace and tranquility.

You will share with me and my plants, this beautiful apartment, located in the Horta neighborhood of Barcelona.

If you are looking for a 5* hotel service and you think that by paying, you have the power to do whatever you want... please don't come to my house... I want to give travelers the opportunity to share and live a local experience, from love and respect as human beings that we are.
neighborhood_overview:
The neighborhood of Horta is, perhaps, one of the corners of Barcelona that still retains its authenticity.

Its privileged position, away from the most central and familiar environments of the city, is allowing its essence and the characteristics that make it unique to continue to remain.

Horta continues to maintain the village air within the big city! It is a “lifelong” neighborhood, where only tourists arrive.
Quiet, safe and authentic area.

Ideal place to rest and visit the city by day. Close to home there is a pharmacy and a "paki" shop that opens from 8h to 22h.

Supermercados a 10 min walk from home, where the subway is.

***ATTENTION* ** Taking the distances as a walk are part of the trip, if you want to have everything close and at your disposal in a minute, sorry to inform you that you will not find it here... In return, you are next to parks and mountains to get lost and discover the REAL BARCELONA.
host_about:
Hola soy Rumi!

Y soy una chica muy abierta de mente, extrovertida, entregada y auténtica. 

Hedonista y sencilla, a la que le gusta mucho el crecimiento personal y espiritual.

Libre de miedos y con pensamiento crítico, me defino como una persona tranquila a la que le gusta estar en casa, dar un buen paseo, leer un buen libro y cocinar bien rico!

Con mucha energía y mucho flow, me gusta conocer gente de todas partes y ayudarles a que se sientan como en casa en una ciudad que no es la suya...

Hablo Inglés, castellano y catalán! Hija de padres argentinos, pero nada y criada en Barcelona, aunque me siento del mundo!

Quiero compartir contigo mi espacio, mi cueva, mi templo. Para que tengas una experiencia familiar y acogedora, dónde te sientas arropado desde el minuto uno, por una persona que no conoces en la ciudad que vas a visitar. Me gustaría que te sientas como en casa, no como un extraño que paga por dormir e irse…

Que podamos compartir momentos y charlas, y que tu estancia pueda fluir de la mejor manera posible, para que sea maravillosa e inolvidable.

¿Te vienes a mi casa y vivir una "Rumi's World Experience"?

host_about:
El entorno dinámico y alegre de la capital catalana se plasma en The Moods Catedral en forma de experiencia de alojamiento cercana y cálida. Desde el trato de nuestro personal hasta la comodidad de la zona común y nuestras 17 habitaciones, todos los ambientes del hostal tienen mucho de Barcelona y del carácter mediterráneo de sus gentes.

Una idiosincrasia que se percibe ya a la llegada a este hotel del barrio Gótico, donde una recepción con techo de volta catalana con ladrillos en blanco y muebles de líneas sencillas en tonos beige dan la bienvenida al visitante. El pavimento textil en tonos tierra a juego con el minimalismo del mobiliario se conjuga a la perfección con paredes blancas no exentas de vegetación y una presencia omnipresente de la madera. El toque final de bienestar lo aportan las cómodas butacas en tela de lino, un lugar donde descansar o tomar algo.

Esta decoración de diseño llena de guiños a la tierra se reproduce a lo largo de todos y cada uno de los espacios. Colores puros, elementos básicos y geometrías simples se repiten en la zona común de este hotel situado en el límite de los barrios del Gótic y el Born.

En esta zona común, a la cual nos gusta llamar Helpyourself por el servicio gratuito de bebidas al cual tienes acceso durante todo el día, encontrarás también una sala donde hojear algunas de nuestras revistas de moda, tomarte algo, trabajar con tu ordenador o simplemente descansar después de una jornada de turismo en la ciudad.

Asimismo, nuestras 17 luminosas y tranquilas habitaciones han sido creadas en un estilo contemporáneo donde la exclusividad no está reñida con la sencillez.

En The Moods Catedral te transportamos a la mismísima esencia del Mediterráneo.

host_about:
We are Abril and Eloi. We are a couple and we are actors- with similar interests.  We like to travel, meet new people from other backgrounds, go to the movies, the theater, museums, watch documentaries, listen to music, going to concerts, reading, dancing, looking after our plants, bike riding (our favorite mode of transportation), trying foods from other countries, cooking mexican-catalan food and  inventing our own dishes. We love to learn new things as well as spending time with our family and friends. We also practice yoga. I am a Hatha Yoga instructor. My partner Eloi enjoys jogging very much.   Whenever we have a free weekend, we spend time in the Costa Brava which is only an hour away from the city. The Costa Brava is known for its lush forrest as well as its pristine beaches. Each autumn, you can find us with baskets at the forrest collecting wild mushrooms to make fabulous meals.  

Being hosts in our home is an opportunity to open the door to new experiences and to gain access to what is happening in other latitudes around the world as well as exchanging ideas and different perspectives. We can learn and enjoy what life has to offer from its vast hues to its lush colors. We would be very happy to show you the beauty of our city and its peoples . Life is about enjoyment and seeing the beauty this world has to offer. Let us be your guide in Barcelona! 


Somos Abril y Eloi, una pareja de actores con intereses muy parecidos. Nos gusta viajar, conocer gente de otras culturas, ir al cine, ir al teatro, museos, ver series, documentales, escuchar música, conciertos, bailar, leer, cuidar de nuestras plantas, andar en bicicleta (nuestro medio de transporte en la ciudad), probar comida de otros lugares, cocinar comida catalo-mexicana e inventar nuevos platillos, estar con la familia, aprender cosas nuevas y disfrutar de los amigos. También practicamos yoga (Abril es profesora de Hatha Yoga) y a Eloi le encanta correr. Cada vez que tenemos oportunidad, generalmente los fines de semana, nos escapamos a la Costa Brava, donde a sólo hora y media de esta ciudad, disfrutamos de sus playas cristalinas y sus bosques (donde cada otoño, nos encontrarás con nuestro cesto bajo el brazo recolectando setas para unas buenas comilonas).
Recibir huéspedes en nuestro hogar, es abrir la puerta a nuevas experiencias, conocer lo que sucede en otras latitudes, intercambiar ideas y visiones distintas, aprender y disfrutar de la vida con sus diversos matices y colores. Estaremos encantados de mostrarte la belleza de nuestra ciudad y su gente. La vida es para disfrutarla plenamente y ver el hermoso mundo en el que vivimos, déjanos ser tu guía en Barcelona!

neighborhood_overview:
Guinardó, in Barcelona, is one of the neighborhoods in the Horta-Guinardó district. Its boundaries are: Passeig de Maragall, Carrer de Sant Antoni Maria Claret, Carrer de Cartagena, and Parc del Guinardó. In the 19th century, it was agricultural with country houses, like Mas Guinardó, which gave its name to the neighborhood. In the early 20th century, it consisted of small houses; in the 60s, it transformed into blocks.

Parc Güell stands out in Guinardó. Covering 15.9 hectares, it's one of Barcelona's largest green spaces, offering magnificent views. The Hospital de Sant Pau, a UNESCO World Heritage site, is another architectural gem. Guinardó is residential, with small homes and low-rise buildings (around €4000/m²). Rent averages around €10/m².

This quiet residential neighborhood is located near Parc Güell and offers convenient connections. Guinardó is ideal for families and those seeking a serene space, even though it has less nightlife compared to other areas.

Its boundaries are: Passeig de Maragall, Carrer de Sant Antoni Maria Claret, Carrer de Cartagena, and Parc del Guinardó. In the 19th century, it was agricultural with country houses, like Mas Guinardó, which gave its name to the neighborhood. In the early 20th century, it consisted of small houses; in the 60s, it transformed into blocks.

Parc Güell stands out in Guinardó. Covering 15.9 hectares, it's one of Barcelona's largest green spaces, offering magnificent views. The Hospital de Sant Pau, a UNESCO World Heritage site, is another architectural gem. Guinardó is residential, with small homes and low-rise buildings (around €4000/m²). Rent averages around €10/m².

name: Cosy bedroom in great location
description:
A comfortable private bedroom with queen size bed in a shared apartment with daily cleaning. Located in the old town of Barcelona.

Discover the lively neighborhood 'El Born'. Walking distance from the beach, the park, the famous Ramblas & more. Easy access to public transportation to visit the main sights of Gaudi.

Fresh sheets, clean towels and more are included. Excellent WIFI. There is a lock on the bedroom door inside & outside.
neighborhood_overview:
Located on the edge of the artistic area 'El Born'. It is a safe and lively area full of bars, restaurants, art galleries, fashionable boutiques, musea, crafts,...

Walking distance from Barceloneta beach (10min), the nightclubs (15min), the most beautiful park of the city (2min) and the famous Ramblas (15min). You are close to public transportation such as buses, the train station and the metro (the yellow line and stop 'Barceloneta').

This neighborhood is known for its history and culture. We recommend going for a walk and getting lost in the small streets with cute boutiques, bars and restaurants with typical Spanish tapas.

The property is within walking distance of the Parc Ciutadella, one of the largest parks in the city, as well as the Picasso Museum and the Palau de la Música Catalana.

In addition, the famous Santa Caterina Market is very close, where guests can enjoy local gastronomy and buy fresh products.

Camp Nou: The FC Barcelona stadium is the main tourist attraction of the neighborhood. If you are a football fan, don't miss the chance to visit this legendary stadium.
Pedralbes Royal Palace: This former royal residence is now home to art and design exhibitions, as well as beautiful gardens where you can walk quietly.
Monasterio de Pedralbes: A magnificent example of Catalan gothic architecture, with a cloister and frescoes that will leave you breathless.

neighborhood_overview:
Barcelona's Gothic Quarter is the city's oldest district, located in the Ciutat Vella district. This charming neighborhood is bounded by Las Ramblas, Vía Laietana, Paseo de Colón and Plaza de Cataluña. Known for its medieval layout of narrow pedestrian streets and hidden squares, the Gothic Quarter invites visitors to explore centuries of history through its ancient monuments and vibrant atmosphere.

What to see in the Gothic Quarter
The Gothic Quarter of Barcelona has numerous tourist attractions for all tastes, among which we could highlight the following:

Santa Eulalia Cathedral: Also known as La Seu, the Cathedral of Barcelona is a famous example of Catalan Gothic architecture dating back to the 14th century.
Plaza Sant Jaume: Political center of Barcelona, it is the place where the Town Hall and the Palace of the Generalitat of Catalonia are located.
Calle del Bisbe: Nice pedestrian street that connects Plaza Sant Jaume with the Cathedral.

Stroll through its pedestrian streets full of neighborhood shops, traditional markets such as the Mercat del Clot, and tree-lined squares perfect for relaxing after a day of exploring.

Very well connected by metro and train (Clot-Aragó), you can reach the city center, the beach or the Sagrada Familia in just a few minutes.

Perfect for those looking to experience Barcelona like a local, El Clot offers the ideal mix of residential calm and proximity to the city's main attractions.
